explanations: inFlight.dec is only called after a successful provider.send. When send throws (rejected or failed), the catch and finally blocks never decrement the gauge, so notifications_in_flight drifts upward by one per failure and never returns to zero. During a provider outage the gauge climbs steadily, triggering false saturation alerts and hiding the real concurrency. The decrement belongs in the finally block.
The catch block checks err instanceof ProviderRejectedError and uses "rejected". "failed" is for other errors, and "sent" only on success.
The worker count is Math.min(concurrency, batch.length) = min(8, 3) = 3.
The check and next++ run synchronously between awaits on a single thread, so no other worker can observe the same index. Promise.all does not create threads, and the cap does not matter to safety.
